γδ T cell-mediated tumor cell lysis is characterized by trafficking of lysosomes and actin reorganization, which is different from the cytotoxic T cell-mediated tumor lysis.

(1) γδ T lymphocytes can recognize tumor cells and form a direct contact with them; (2) γδ T cells release the lysosome components into the tumor cells, leading to the tumor cell death; (3) γδ T cell receptors are evenly distributed in the cell membrane and not accumulated in the effector/target contact area.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the trafficking of lysosomes and the reorganization of actins and T cell receptors in gammadeltaT lymphocytes while they are killing tumor cells.
the trafficking of lysosomes and the distribution of T-cell receptors and actin filaments during the process of tumor killing of γδT cells.
the trafficking of lysosomes and the redistribution of TCR and cytoskeletal proteins in γδT cells when killing tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the γδ T cells kill tumor cell by lysosome exocytosis and reorganize of actin filaments and redistribute of T cell receptors during the process of tumor cell killing.
the γδ T cell can kill the tumor cells by direct contact and the release of lysosomal contents.
the γδ T cells can kill the MeWo cells through direct cell contact.

the trafficking of lysosomes and the reorganization of actins together with the redistribution T cell receptors (TCR) play an important role in the γδT lymphocyte mediated tumor cell killing.
